evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Partner with the Data Hub Team to ensure development adheres to standards and utilizes the latest technologies, ensuring data quality, compliance, and security are in place at launch and maintained over time.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities repeatedly emphasize data quality, compliance, security, and best practices with no velocity/speed language, placing this at rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: ensuring data quality, compliance, and security are in place at launch and maintained over time
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Compliance is named but generically, without financial-reporting or regulatory-audit specifics, and the sector/client context is unstated, placing this at moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: data scientists; analysts; business teams; Data Hub Team
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A 'Data Hub Team' with existing standards is named as a partner, indicating an established but growing data function rather than a from-zero build.
evidence.jd_authorship: Work with modern cloud-based data architectures, including data Lakehouse, to ensure security, scalability, reliability, and cost-effective data storage and processing.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Despite naming specific tools (Snowflake, dbt, Airflow), the bullets are generic consulting-boilerplate phrasing ('drive innovation', 'at the forefront of the industry', 'translate business needs into efficient data solutions') that could describe almost any data engineering role, characteristic of recruiter-authored consulting postings.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including data scientists, analysts, and business teams, to translate business needs into efficient data solutions.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on building data products and pipelines for internal data consumers (data scientists, analysts) rather than one specific commercial, product, or finance audience.
evidence.autonomy_level: shaping the architecture, processes, and strategies of our analytics ecosystem
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The intro claims strategic architecture-shaping scope, but the itemized responsibilities are execution-level (build, optimize, implement), making this mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: AI/ML tools appear only as a junior-level 'nice to have' requirement, not an expectation placed on the candidate's own workflow or infrastructure output.
evidence.testing_framing: Implement best practices for data quality and performance.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality is named as a responsibility area but without a specific testing framework or ownership verb tied to a named tool, more general practice than a concrete testing responsibility.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: ensuring data quality, compliance, and security are in place at launch and maintained over time
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Compliance and security are named as ongoing concerns secondary to delivery, without regulatory or stakeholder-trust framing dominating, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Design, develop, and optimize data products, data models, and pipelines
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The JD mixes new-build verbs (design, develop) with optimization verbs (optimize, streamline, maintain) roughly evenly, making this mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: ensuring data quality, compliance, and security are in place at launch and maintained over time — a secondary operational concern, not a dominant risk register.
